mechanism_narrative: The four-week collapse in TRANSIT (from -33.6 to -60.7) removes commuting and discretionary trips that feed retail and recreation venues; because transit use and retail footfall co-move, RETAIL_REC continues lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell 27.1 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is equal to or higher than its mean over the last 28 days while TRANSIT remains below -50.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility above +15 signals stay-at-home compliance; each additional point of RESIDENTIAL above +15 reduces out-of-home retail trips, so RETAIL_REC falls further over two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next 14 days even though RESIDENTIAL remains above +15.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction of TRANSIT below -50 and GROCERY_PHARM below -15 marks a broad withdrawal from routine errands; retail-and-recreation trips are the most discretionary component and therefore decline more than either series alone predicts over four weeks.
failure_condition: When TRANSIT is below -50 and GROCERY_PHARM below -15, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not lower than its prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Workplace closures below -30 proxy for enforced containment; as WORKPLACES stay below -30, policy keeps retail non-essential, so RETAIL_REC remains depressed over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds its last 28-day mean while WORKPLACES stays below -30.

mechanism_narrative: A further week-on-week drop in TRANSIT of more than 10 points signals new movement restrictions; such tightening immediately suppresses retail-and-recreation mobility within one week and keeps it negative over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell 7.7 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: After a week-on-week TRANSIT drop greater than 10 points, RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than its last 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS below -20 indicates that even outdoor leisure is curtailed; when PARKS and RESIDENTIAL move in opposite directions, residents substitute home activity for all out-of-home activity, depressing RETAIL_REC over one week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell to -32.4 and RESIDENTIAL rose to 19.4
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is not lower than its last 7-day mean when PARKS < -20 and RESIDENTIAL > 15.

mechanism_narrative: Early-spring seasonal norms would lift PARKS and retail footfall, but the current PARKS collapse shows the seasonal channel is overridden; RETAIL_REC therefore stays below its prior four-week mean over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is equal to or higher than its last 28-day mean while PARKS remains below -20.

mechanism_narrative: A deceleration in the TRANSIT decline signals that the mobility shock is bottoming; once TRANSIT stops falling week-on-week, pent-up retail demand produces a higher RETAIL_REC mean over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT decline slowed from 11.9 points to 7.7 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than its last 28-day mean after TRANSIT records a week-on-week change of zero or positive.
